target_claim: The reduction's Claim 1: H is 3-colorable if and only if the constructed river-crossing instance (n=3m, k=m+1, G with same-vertex-copy edges and (u(i),v(i)) edges) admits a valid crossing sequence.
source_quote:
Claim 1. H is 3-colorable if and only if there exists a valid crossing sequence for the con-
structed instance.
test_sketch: Implement the construction verbatim (three copies per vertex; edges {(u(i),v(j)): (u,v) in EH, i=j} union {(v(i),v(j)): i!=j}; k=m+1) plus a brute-force BFS oracle over states (L,R,c) enforcing the stated validity/transition rules. Input family: small 3-colorable graphs, e.g. H=K2 (m=2), giving n=6, k=3. BFS shows NO valid crossing sequence exists: after any first trip carrying at most k-1=2 passengers, the left bank (Charon absent) still holds >=4 of the 6 copies, so some vertex retains two of its three copies, which are enemies by construction, so no first move is valid. Yet K2 is 3-colorable, refuting the forward direction of Claim 1. (Consistently, the paper's forward-direction schedule only transports C1 u C2 u C3 = m of the 3m passengers, never reaching the goal state.)
